shloka_text: तच्छ्रुत्वा हर्षमापेदे राघवो भ्रातृभिः सह । वाक्यं चाद्भुतसङ्काशं तदा प्रोवाच लक्ष्मणम् ।। 7.102.1 ।।
transliteration: tacchrutvā harṣamāpede rāghavo bhrātṛbhiḥ saha | vākyaṃ cādbhutasaṅkāśaṃ tadā provāca lakṣmaṇam || 7.102.1 ||
translation: तत् that, श्रुत्वा having heard, हर्षम् joy, आपेदे attained, राघवः Rama, भ्रातृभिः with brothers, सह together, वाक्यम् words, च and, अद्भुतसङ्काशम् wonderful-like, तदा then, प्रोवाच spoke, लक्ष्मणम् to Lakshmana.
explanation: Having heard that, Rama, along with his brothers, felt great joy and then spoke amazing words to Lakshmana.
comments: Rama resolves to give kingdoms to Lakshmana's sons Angada and Chandraketu, settling them at Bharata's counsel in the peaceful Karupatha land -- he founds Angadiya for Angada and Chandrakanta in the Malla country for Chandraketu, whom Lakshmana and Bharata escort to their realms before returning -- and ten thousand years pass, the three brothers shining like three sacred fires.

shloka_text: इमौ कुमारौ सौमित्रे तव धर्मविशारदौ । अङ्गदश्चन्द्रकेतुश्च राज्यार्थे दृढविक्रमौ ।। 7.102.2 ।।
transliteration: imau kumārau saumitre tava dharmaviśāradau | aṅgadaścandraketuśca rājyārthe dṛḍhavikramau || 7.102.2 ||
translation: इमौ these two, कुमारौ sons, सौमित्रे O Lakshmana, तव your, धर्मविशारदौ expert in righteousness, अङ्गदः Angada, चन्द्रकेतुः Chandraketu, च and, राज्यार्थे for the sake of kingdom, दृढविक्रमौ of firm valor.
explanation: O Lakshmana, these two sons of yours, Angada and Chandraketu, are skilled in righteousness and possess firm valor suitable for kingship.

shloka_text: इमौ राज्ये ऽभिषेक्ष्यामि देशः साधु विधीयताम् । रमणीयो ह्यसम्बाधो रमेतां यत्र धन्विनौ ।। 7.102.3 ।।
transliteration: imau rājye 'bhiṣekṣyāmi deśaḥ sādhu vidhīyatām | ramaṇīyo hyasambādho rametāṃ yatra dhanvinau || 7.102.3 ||
translation: इमौ these two, राज्ये in the kingdom, अभिषेक्ष्यामि I shall enthrone, देशः a region, साधु properly, विधीयताम् let it be arranged, रमणीयः charming, हि indeed, असम्बाधः unobstructed, रमेताम् let them dwell happily, यत्र where, धन्विनौ the two archers.
explanation: I shall enthrone these two in a kingdom, so let a suitable, charming, and unobstructed region be prepared where these two archers can happily reside.

shloka_text: न राज्ञो यत्र पीडा स्यान्नाश्रमाणां विनाशनम् । स देशो दृश्यतां सौम्य नापराध्यामहे यथा ।। 7.102.4 ।।
transliteration: na rājño yatra pīḍā syānnāśramāṇāṃ vināśanam | sa deśo dṛśyatāṃ saumya nāparādhyāmahe yathā || 7.102.4 ||
translation: न not, राज्ञः of the king, यत्र where, पीडा suffering, स्यात् may be, न not, आश्रमाणां of the hermitages, विनाशनम् destruction, सः that, देशः region, दृश्यताम् let it be found, सौम्य O gentle one, न not, अपराध्यामहे we may err, यथा so that.
explanation: O gentle one, let a region be found where there is no oppression of kings or destruction of hermitages, so that we may not commit any fault.

shloka_text: तथोक्तवति रामे तु भरतः प्रत्युवाच ह । अयं कारुपथो देशो रमणीयो निरामयः ।। 7.102.5 ।।
transliteration: tathoktavati rāme tu bharataḥ pratyuvāca ha | ayaṃ kārupatho deśo ramaṇīyo nirāmayaḥ || 7.102.5 ||
translation: तथा thus, उक्तवति having spoken, रामे when Rama, तु indeed, भरतः Bharata, प्रत्युवाच replied, ह indeed, अयम् this, कारुपथः Karupatha, देशः region, रमणीयः charming, निरामयः peaceful.
explanation: When Rama had thus spoken, Bharata replied, "This region called Karupatha is charming and peaceful."

shloka_text: निवेश्यतां तत्र पुरमङ्गदस्य महात्मनः । चन्द्रकेतोः सुरुचिरं चन्द्रकान्तं निरामयम् ।। 7.102.6 ।।
transliteration: niveśyatāṃ tatra puramaṅgadasya mahātmanaḥ | candraketoḥ suruciraṃ candrakāntaṃ nirāmayam || 7.102.6 ||
translation: निवेश्यतां let it be established, तत्र there, पुरम् a city, अङ्गदस्य of Angada, महात्मनः the great-souled one, चन्द्रकेतोः of Chandraketu, सुरुचिरम् very beautiful, चन्द्रकान्तम् charming like the moon (or named Chandrakanta), निरामयम् free from disease.
explanation: Let a city be established there for the great-souled Angada and another, very beautiful, moon-charming, and healthy city for Chandraketu.

shloka_text: तद्वाक्यं भरतेनोक्तं प्रतिजग्राह राघवः । तं च कृत्वा वशे देशमङ्गदस्य न्यवेशयत् ।। 7.102.7 ।।
transliteration: tadvākyaṃ bharatenoktaṃ pratijagrāha rāghavaḥ | taṃ ca kṛtvā vaśe deśamaṅgadasya nyaveśayat || 7.102.7 ||
translation: तत् that, वाक्यम् statement, भरतेन by Bharata, उक्तम् spoken, प्रतिजग्राह accepted, राघवः Rama, तम् that, च and, कृत्वा having made, वशे under control, देशम् region, अङ्गदस्य for Angada, न्यवेशयत् he established.
explanation: Rama accepted that statement spoken by Bharata, and having brought that region under control, he established a city for Angada.

shloka_text: अङ्गदीया पुरी रम्याप्यङ्गदस्य निवेशिता । रमणीया सुगुप्ता च रामेणाक्लिष्टकर्मणा ।। 7.102.8 ।।
transliteration: aṅgadīyā purī ramyāpyaṅgadasya niveśitā | ramaṇīyā suguptā ca rāmeṇākliṣṭakarmaṇā || 7.102.8 ||
translation: अङ्गदीया Angada's, पुरी city, रम्या beautiful, अपि also, अङ्गदस्य for Angada, निवेशिता established, रमणीया delightful, सुगुप्ता well-protected, च and, रामेण by Rama, अक्लिष्टकर्मणा whose deeds are effortless.
explanation: The beautiful city named Angadiya was established for Angada by Rama, whose deeds are effortless, and it was delightful and well-protected.

shloka_text: चन्द्रकेतोश्च मल्लस्य मल्लभूम्यां निवेशिता । चन्द्रकान्तेति विख्याता दिव्या स्वर्गपुरी यथा ।। 7.102.9 ।।
transliteration: candraketośca mallasya mallabhūmyāṃ niveśitā | candrakānteti vikhyātā divyā svargapurī yathā || 7.102.9 ||
translation: चन्द्रकेतोः for Chandraketu, च and, मल्लस्य of Malla, मल्लभूम्याम् in the land of Malla, निवेशिता established, चन्द्रकान्ता Chandrakanta, इति thus, विख्याता renowned, दिव्या divine, स्वर्गपुरी a city of heaven, यथा like.
explanation: And for Chandraketu, a city named Chandrakanta was established in the land of Malla, renowned as divine, just like a city of heaven.

shloka_text: ततो रामः परां प्रीतिं लक्ष्मणो भरतस्तथा । ययुर्युद्धे दुराधर्षा अभिषेकं च चक्रिरे ।। 7.102.10 ।।
transliteration: tato rāmaḥ parāṃ prītiṃ lakṣmaṇo bharatastathā | yayuryuddhe durādharṣā abhiṣekaṃ ca cakrire || 7.102.10 ||
translation: ततः then, रामः Rama, परां great, प्रीतिम् joy, लक्ष्मणः Lakshmana, भरतः Bharata, तथा and, ययुः attained, युद्धे in battle, दुराधर्षाः unconquerable, अभिषेकं anointment, च and, चक्रिरे they performed.
explanation: Then Rama, Lakshmana, and Bharata, who were unconquerable in battle, attained great joy and performed the anointment.

shloka_text: अभिषिच्य कुमारौ स प्रस्थापयति राघवः । अङ्गदं पश्चिमां भूमिं चन्द्रकेतुमुदङ्मुखम् ।। 7.102.11 ।।
transliteration: abhiṣicya kumārau sa prasthāpayati rāghavaḥ | aṅgadaṃ paścimāṃ bhūmiṃ candraketumudaṅmukham || 7.102.11 ||
translation: अभिषिच्य having consecrated, कुमारौ the two princes, स he, प्रस्थापयति sends forth, राघवः Rama, अङ्गदं Angada, पश्चिमां to the western, भूमिं land, चन्द्रकेतुं Chandraketu, उदङ्मुखम् to the northern direction.
explanation: Having consecrated the two princes, Rama sent Angada to the western region and Chandraketu to the northern direction.

shloka_text: अङ्गदं चापि सौमित्रिर्लक्ष्मणो ऽनुजगाम ह । चन्द्रकेतोस्तु भरतः पार्ष्णिग्राहो बभूव ह ।। 7.102.12 ।।
transliteration: aṅgadaṃ cāpi saumitrirlakṣmaṇo 'nujagāma ha | candraketostu bharataḥ pārṣṇigrāho babhūva ha || 7.102.12 ||
translation: अङ्गदं Angada, च and, अपि also, सौमित्रिः Lakshmana, लक्ष्मणः Lakshmana, अनुजगाम followed, ह indeed, चन्द्रकेतोस्तु but for Chandraketu, भरतः Bharata, पार्ष्णिग्राहो a supporter, बभूव became, ह indeed.
explanation: Lakshmana, the son of Sumitra, followed Angada, and Bharata became Chandraketu's close supporter.

shloka_text: लक्ष्मणस्त्वङ्गदीयायां संवत्सरमथोषितः । पुत्रे स्थिते दुराधर्षे अयोध्यां पुनरागमत् ।। 7.102.13 ।।
transliteration: lakṣmaṇastvaṅgadīyāyāṃ saṃvatsaramathoṣitaḥ | putre sthite durādharṣe ayodhyāṃ punarāgamat || 7.102.13 ||
translation: लक्ष्मणस्तु but Lakshmana, अङ्गदीयायां in Angada's territory, संवत्सरम् for a year, अथ then, उषितः having resided, पुत्रे his son, स्थिते having been established, दुराधर्षे unconquerable, अयोध्यां to Ayodhya, पुनः again, आगमत् returned.
explanation: Lakshmana, having resided for a year in Angada's territory until his unconquerable son was established, then returned to Ayodhya.

shloka_text: भरतो ऽपि तथैवोष्य संवत्सरमतो ऽधिकम् । अयोध्यां पुनरागम्य रामपादावुपास्त सः ।। 7.102.14 ।।
transliteration: bharato 'pi tathaivoṣya saṃvatsaramato 'dhikam | ayodhyāṃ punarāgamya rāmapādāvupāsta saḥ || 7.102.14 ||
translation: भरतो Bharata, अपि also, तथैव similarly, उष्य having resided, संवत्सरम् for a year, अतः than that, अधिकम् more, अयोध्यां to Ayodhya, पुनः again, आगम्य having returned, रामपादावुपास्त worshipped Rama's feet, सः he.
explanation: Bharata also, having similarly resided for more than a year, returned to Ayodhya and worshipped Rama's feet.

shloka_text: उभौ सौमित्रिभरतौ रामपादावनुव्रतौ । कालं गतमपि स्नेहान्न जज्ञाते ऽतिधार्मिकौ ।। 7.102.15 ।।
transliteration: ubhau saumitribharatau rāmapādāvanuvratau | kālaṃ gatamapi snehānna jajñāte 'tidhārmikau || 7.102.15 ||
translation: उभौ both, सौमित्रिभरतौ Lakshmana and Bharata, रामपादावनुव्रतौ devoted to Rama's feet, कालं time, गतमपि even passed, स्नेहात् due to affection, न not, जज्ञाते they knew, अतिधार्मिकौ extremely righteous.
explanation: Both Lakshmana and Bharata, being extremely righteous and devoted to Rama's feet, did not even perceive the passage of time due to their profound affection.

shloka_text: एवं वर्षसहस्राणि दश तेषां ययुस्तदा । धर्मे प्रयतमानानां पौरकार्येषु नित्यदा ।। 7.102.16 ।।
transliteration: evaṃ varṣasahasrāṇi daśa teṣāṃ yayustadā | dharme prayatamānānāṃ paurakāryeṣu nityadā || 7.102.16 ||
translation: एवं thus, वर्षसहस्राणि thousands of years, दश ten, तेषां of them, ययुः passed, तदा then, धर्मे in righteousness, प्रयतमानानां of those striving, पौरकार्येषु in civic duties, नित्यदा always.
explanation: Thus, ten thousand years passed for them, who were constantly striving in righteousness and civic duties.

shloka_text: विहृत्य कालं परिपूर्णमानसाः श्रिया वृता धर्मपुरे सुसंस्थिताः । त्रयः समिद्धा इव दीप्ततेजसो महाध्वरे साधु हुतास्त्रयो ऽग्नयः ।। 7.102.17 ।।
transliteration: vihṛtya kālaṃ paripūrṇamānasāḥ śriyā vṛtā dharmapure susaṃsthitāḥ | trayaḥ samiddhā iva dīptatejaso mahādhvare sādhu hutāstrayo 'gnayaḥ || 7.102.17 ||
translation: विहृत्य having spent, कालं time, परिपूर्णमानसाः with minds completely satisfied, श्रिया with prosperity, वृताः endowed, धर्मपुरे in the city of dharma, सुसंस्थिताः well-established, त्रयः the three, समिद्धाः well-kindled, इव like, दीप्ततेजसः of blazing splendor, महाध्वरे in a great sacrifice, साधु properly, हुताः offered, त्रयः three, अग्नयः fires.
explanation: Having spent their time with fulfilled desires, endowed with prosperity, and well-established in the city of dharma, the three brothers shone like three well-kindled fires of blazing splendor, properly offered in a great sacrifice. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे व्द्युत्तरशततमः सर्गः ।। 102 ।। Thus ends the hundred and second sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
